NCCL kernel intervals can include synchronization; intersection is temporal coexistence only.
Fused peer kernels have no separate NCCL interval: absence cannot imply absence of communication.
Cross-device sums are not wall-clock latency, physical bandwidth, or causal communication hiding.
Register/shared-memory declarations are per-kernel resource requirements, not achieved occupancy.
